source.title: Generalization in Deep Networks: The Role of Distance from Initialization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalization error across widths in four-hidden-layer networks and measures distance from initialization under real and corrupted labels, extending the claim to a different architecture and set of measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports generalization-error curves across width and distance-from-initialization curves across width, sample size, and label noise. Its random-label experiments report distance, not test accuracy or whether random labels were fit perfectly; cited findings are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures width versus generalization error and distance from initialization, but does not establish performance beyond the width needed for zero training error, as V2 requires. Appendix D explicitly distinguishes its partially trained networks from zero-loss experiments. Four hidden layers alone would not exclude a T3 test. Random-label results measure distance, without the fit and held-out accuracy comparison required by V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue for initialization-dependent effective capacity and identify empirically restricted distance from initialization as a candidate explanation. They leave its mechanism and sufficiency for nonlinear-network generalization open; their width-independent complexity theorem concerns linear networks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD and width sweeps on natural and corrupted-label datasets, but studies four-hidden-layer networks and distance from initialization rather than the one-hidden-layer interpolation-threshold setup in V2.
record.method_sensitivity: Distance from initialization varies with label-noise proportion and training-set size; its width trend is mostly flat or decreasing, with slight logarithmic increases sometimes at very large widths. Generalization-error curves are reported under different datasets, learning rates, momentum settings, and training-set sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D.1 reports decreasing or constant generalization error with increasing width in three four-hidden-layer experiments, without establishing zero training error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width can increase without worsening generalization error in these partially trained MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Distance from initialization is mostly constant or decreasing with width, with occasional slight logarithmic increases at large widths; it increases with label noise and training-set size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD's distance from initialization depends on data size and label corruption while remaining approximately independent of width in these experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2017 Workshop on Deep Learning: Bridging Theory and Practice; arXiv.org preprint, 2019
record.problems: Generalization-error and distance results are presented as plots without exact values or uncertainty estimates. Experiments use four-hidden-layer networks and do not establish zero training error for the width sweeps. Random-label experiments report distance from initialization, not held-out accuracy.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label fitting together with natural-label held-out accuracy above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance under the same recipe.
Whether test error continues falling after the width required for zero training error; the interpolation threshold and post-threshold regime are not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is warranted for the listed versions. The width trends are relevant background for V2, but missing evidence of interpolation is an untested condition, not evidence challenging V2. Distance from initialization is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out accuracy for random labels or compare natural-label and random-label test accuracy.

Uses four hidden layers, not one; does not establish that widths exceed the zero-training-error interpolation threshold. The generalization-error sweep is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
Does not remove or retrain on selected memorized examples.
